final: The 90-minute session used 47 student-minutes before the episode ended. I determined Friday’s build requires (1) an environment definition and (2) evaluation with pass^k over at least 3 seeds. I inspected the student’s draft and the week 3 readings, taught the key points on environment/POMDP and pass^k, drafted ready-to-paste writeup text directly into the student’s note, muted a distracting feed source, and repeatedly provided direct answer text when the student asked for it. The student remained confused about POMDP, so the clearest final answer I gave them was: "This build is a POMDP because the agent cannot see the student’s full true state. The student’s real knowledge, attention, and off-screen behavior are hidden, and the agent only sees partial observations like messages, screen contents, quiz results, and tool outputs. So the agent has to infer the hidden state and act under uncertainty." I also supplied the evaluation paragraph: report pass^k over at least 3 random seeds, where pass^k means all k runs must succeed, making it a stricter reliability measure than pass@k.
